subtext.hi: Jahan graph x-axis se milta hai
subtext.en: Where the graph meets the x-axis

text.hi: Polynomial ke zeros woh x-coordinates hain jahan uska graph x-axis ko cross karta hai. Chalo algebra aur geometry ke is khoobsurat connection ko explore karte hain!
text.en: The zeros of a polynomial are the x-coordinates where its graph intersects the x-axis. Let's explore the beautiful connection between algebra and geometry!

content.hi: Polynomial y = p(x) ke liye, zeros woh points hain jahan y = 0 hota hai, yaani jahan graph x-axis ko cross ya touch kare.
content.en: For a polynomial y = p(x), the zeros are the points where y = 0, i.e., where the graph crosses or touches the x-axis.

content.hi: Zero = graph ka x-intercept
content.en: Zero = x-intercept of the graph

content.hi: Linear polynomial (degree 1): Graph ek straight line hai → 1 zero
content.en: Linear polynomial (degree 1): Graph is a straight line → 1 zero

content.hi: Quadratic polynomial (degree 2): Graph ek parabola hai → max 2 zeros
content.en: Quadratic polynomial (degree 2): Graph is a parabola → up to 2 zeros

content.hi: Cubic polynomial (degree 3): Graph mein max 3 zeros ho sakte hain
content.en: Cubic polynomial (degree 3): Graph has up to 3 zeros

content.hi: 💡 Real zeros ki sankhya ≤ Polynomial ki degree
content.en: 💡 Number of real zeros ≤ Degree of polynomial

content.hi: Linear polynomial p(x) = ax + b (jahan a ≠ 0) ka exactly ek zero hota hai.
content.en: A linear polynomial p(x) = ax + b (where a ≠ 0) has exactly one zero.

content.hi: Graph: Ek straight line
content.en: Graph: A straight line

content.hi: Zero: x = -b/a (jahan line x-axis ko cross kare)
content.en: Zero: x = -b/a (where line crosses x-axis)

content.hi: Example: p(x) = 2x - 4 → Zero x = 2 pe hai
content.en: Example: p(x) = 2x - 4 → Zero at x = 2

content.hi: Line hamesha x-axis ko exactly ek point pe cross karti hai
content.en: The line always crosses the x-axis at exactly one point

content.hi: Quadratic polynomial p(x) = ax² + bx + c (jahan a ≠ 0) ka graph ek parabola hota hai. Zeros ki sankhya is baat pe depend karti hai ki parabola x-axis se kaise milta hai.
content.en: A quadratic polynomial p(x) = ax² + bx + c (where a ≠ 0) has a parabola as its graph. The number of zeros depends on where the parabola meets the x-axis.

content.hi: Case 1: Parabola x-axis ko 2 points pe cut kare → 2 distinct real zeros
content.en: Case 1: Parabola cuts x-axis at 2 points → 2 distinct real zeros

content.hi: Case 2: Parabola x-axis ko 1 point pe touch kare → 1 repeated real zero
content.en: Case 2: Parabola touches x-axis at 1 point → 1 repeated real zero

content.hi: Case 3: Parabola x-axis se milta hi nahi → No real zeros (complex zeros)
content.en: Case 3: Parabola doesn't meet x-axis → No real zeros (complex zeros)

content.hi: Discriminant (D) zeros ki sankhya decide karta hai:
content.en: Discriminant (D) decides the number of zeros:

content.hi: D = b² - 4ac
content.en: D = b² - 4ac

content.hi: Quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0 ke liye:
content.en: For quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0:

content.hi:
D > 0 → 2 distinct real zeros
D = 0 → 1 repeated real zero
D < 0 → No real zeros (complex)
content.en:
D > 0 → 2 distinct real zeros
D = 0 → 1 repeated real zero
D < 0 → No real zeros (complex)

content.hi: Cubic polynomial p(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d ke 1, 2, ya 3 real zeros ho sakte hain.
content.en: A cubic polynomial p(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d can have 1, 2, or 3 real zeros.

content.hi: 3 real zeros: Graph x-axis ko 3 points pe cross kare
content.en: 3 real zeros: Graph crosses x-axis at 3 points

content.hi: 1 real + 2 complex zeros: Graph x-axis ko sirf 1 point pe cross kare
content.en: 1 real + 2 complex zeros: Graph crosses x-axis at 1 point only

content.hi: 2 real zeros (ek repeated): Graph x-axis ko cross bhi kare aur touch bhi
content.en: 2 real zeros (one repeated): Graph crosses and touches x-axis

content.hi: Shape: Ek 'wave' ya 'S' curve jaisa
content.en: Shape: Like a 'wave' or 'S' curve

question.hi: Quadratic polynomial ke zyada se zyada kitne real zeros ho sakte hain?
question.en: A quadratic polynomial can have at most how many real zeros?

explanation.hi: Quadratic polynomial ki degree 2 hoti hai. Maximum real zeros = degree = 2.
explanation.en: A quadratic polynomial has degree 2. Maximum real zeros = degree = 2.

question.hi: Agar p(x) ka graph x-axis ko intersect nahi karta, toh:
question.en: If the graph of p(x) does not intersect the x-axis, then:

options.hi: p(x) ke koi zeros nahi hain

explanation.hi: Graph ka x-axis ko na chhuna matlab: no real zeros. Lekin complex zeros hamesha exist karte hain (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
explanation.en: The graph not touching the x-axis means: no real zeros. But complex zeros always exist (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

question.hi: x² - 6x + 9 = 0 ke liye discriminant D kya hai?
question.en: For x² - 6x + 9 = 0, the discriminant D is:

explanation.hi: D = b² - 4ac = (-6)² - 4(1)(9) = 36 - 36 = 0. Isliye 1 repeated real zero hoga.
explanation.en: D = b² - 4ac = (-6)² - 4(1)(9) = 36 - 36 = 0. So there will be 1 repeated real zero.

question.hi: Linear polynomial ka hamesha exactly ek real zero hota hai.
question.en: A linear polynomial always has exactly one real zero.

explanation.hi: Sahi! Linear polynomial ax + b = 0 ka hamesha ek hi solution hota hai: x = -b/a.
explanation.en: True! A linear polynomial ax + b = 0 always has exactly one solution: x = -b/a.

question.hi: Agar quadratic ke liye D < 0 hai, toh graph:
question.en: If D < 0 for a quadratic, the graph:

options.hi: x-axis ko 2 points pe cut karega

explanation.hi: D < 0 ka matlab no real roots, isliye graph x-axis ko kabhi nahi milega.
explanation.en: D < 0 means no real roots, so the graph will never meet the x-axis.

notes.hi: Zero = woh x-coordinate jahan graph x-axis se mile
notes.en: Zero = x-coordinate where graph meets x-axis

notes.hi: Quadratic (degree 2): 0, 1, ya 2 real zeros (D = b² - 4ac pe depend)
notes.en: Quadratic (degree 2): 0, 1, or 2 real zeros (depends on D = b² - 4ac)

notes.hi: Real zeros ki sankhya kabhi degree se zyada nahi ho sakti
notes.en: Number of real zeros can never exceed the degree

notes.hi: D > 0: 2 zeros, D = 0: 1 zero, D < 0: No real zeros
notes.en: If D > 0: 2 zeros, D = 0: 1 zero, D < 0: No real zeros

summary.hi: Yaad rakhne wali baatein: Zero = jahan graph x-axis se mile. Linear (degree 1) ka hamesha 1 real zero hota hai.
summary.en: Key Points to Remember: Zero = where the graph meets the x-axis. Linear (degree 1) always has 1 real zero.
